A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 6:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Perkins.

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Bird, Rea, Goodhart, Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey,
  Mayor Perkins

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Hoefgen, City Attorney Pannone

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  City Treasurer Sherwood, Minutes Secretary Monson

MAYOR’S REPORT – Matters of Community Interest

Mayor Perkins administered the Oath of Loyalty to the Disaster District Plan (DDP) leaders and
Neighborhood Amateur Radio Team (NART) members which is required to become official Disaster
Service Workers.

Area G Disaster Coordinator Mike Martinet thanked the City Council, City Manager, Police Chief,
John Douglass and the volunteers for their efforts.

Each Councilmember thanked the DDP and NART members for their service to the residents of PVE.

Bryant Winchell chairman of NART announced that more radio operators are needed and a training
class will be held at the end of January.

Mayor Perkins asked the Council to move Item 9 (authorizing purchase of disaster supply containers)
up on the Agenda.
CITY COUNCIL  1
JANUARY 13, 2010
 AUTHORIZATION FOR EXPENDITURE OF $20,970 FOR PROCUREMENT OF SIX
DISASTER DISTRICT PLAN SUPPLY CONTAINERS AND CORRESPONDING
RESOLUTION ADOPTION FOR BUDGET ADJUSTMENT

Police Chief Dreiling reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District had previously
approved the City locating six 20-foot storage containers on the six school sites within the City. This
item is for the purchase of the six containers which will hold emergency supplies to be used by the
Disaster Districts during an emergency. The low bid from Aztec Containers, including shelving, is for
$20,970.

Councilmember Goodhart asked if there is a policy in place to keep track of the supply inventory and
replacement dates for the perishables within the containers. Chief Dreiling responded that there is a
schedule in place. The Chief said the Police Department will be responsible for the containers.

Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey asked where interested parties should send their money donations. Chief
Dreiling said checks should be made out to Palos Verdes Peninsula CERT which has the tax-exempt
account.

There was discussion about the wording of the previously approved License Agreement with regard to
abandonment of the container. It was clarified that this provision allows the School District to deal
with the container if it is abandoned.

It was moved by Councilmember Bird, seconded by Councilmember Goodhart, and unanimously
approved to adopt Resolution R10-02 authorizing an FY 09-10 budget adjustment in the amount of
$20,970 and approve the purchase, readying, and positioning of six 20-foot storage containers to be
located at each of the six PVPUSD schools in the City of Palos Verdes Estates.

Chief Dreiling said the next step would be to place the containers at the school sites and purchase the
supplies for the containers. He suggested a ribbon cutting ceremony at each container site to introduce
the DDP leader in each of the six district areas. The City’s disaster plan is three plans in one: the main
city-wide Emergency Operations Center (EOC), the six District EOCs, and the individual plan which is
called Get Ready, Get Certified. He thanked former Mayor Dwight Abbott for organizing the Get
Ready, Get Certified plan.

Mayor Perkins reminded residents that the Mayors’ Community Forum will be held on Tuesday,
February 2nd, at 6:30pm in the Council Chambers.

NEW BUSINESS

PRESENTATION OF MALAGA COVE GROUNDWATER BENEFICIAL REUSE STUDY

Director Rigg reported that groundwater in and around Malaga Cove Plaza has been a significant issue
for many years. There has been an increase in the number and frequency of sinkholes caused by water
intrusion in underground utilities and well as electrical failures due to water filling the underground
facilities. Due to complex geology issues, groundwater concentrates near the surface in the Malaga
Cove Plaza area. The source of the water has been studied and believed to be a combination of rainfall
and irrigation. In the 1970’s wells were installed behind the Bank of America building to alleviate
problems due to the groundwater. In 1993 the City installed a groundwater monitoring well. In 1993
the groundwater reached a very high level and caused the City to develop an emergency mitigation
plan. The City drilled nine wells to be used to provide immediate relief for the buildings and to study
the groundwater. The pumps were able to take a lot of the groundwater, but this was seen as a short-
term solution due to the limited impact on the groundwater, the cost of electricity, and the need for
maintenance. The City’s geologist at the time recommended that the best long-term solution would be
the installation of a perforated sub-drain. There were problems with the installation due to caving,
contractor problems, and the 14 foot depth of the drain in a very tight area (alley). When the pipe was
first installed in conveyed approximately 650,000 gallons per day – which is a large amount.
Approximately six years ago a large sink hole was discovered at the intersection of Via Chico and Via
Campesina. This is one of many sinkholes. The groundwater continually pushes into the buildings and
the City utilities. There had not been a comprehensive groundwater analysis for the MC Plaza. In an
effort to try to remedy the issues in the MC Plaza and possibly discover beneficial uses for the
groundwater, the West Basin Water District jointly funded, with the Water Replenishment District, a
study to determine if the water from MC Plaza could be extracted and utilized at the Golf Course for
irrigation. The final report from RMC Water Environment is what is being presented this evening for
Council review. The analysis includes an analysis of the ground water quality, volume, potential users,
fatal flaw analysis, and financial analysis. RMC looked at moving the water down to Malaga Cove

CITY COUNCIL  7
JANUARY 13, 2010
 School as well as through the sand dunes over to the Golf Course. The hope was that it would be less
expensive to convey the groundwater to the Golf Course and/or the Malaga Cove School. It turned out
the cost of conveying the groundwater is two to three times more expensive than using potable water.
It would be less expensive if the extraction point were closer to the end use. The Golf Club is
investigating this possibility. The groundwater problems continue in Malaga Cove Plaza. The Council
may want to decide whether to further study the groundwater and/or potential other remedies to
manage the groundwater in MC Plaza, if at all.

Councilmember Bird asked if the Golf Club were to drill a well for extracting groundwater, would we
expect a reduction in groundwater in MC Plaza. Director Rigg said that is unknown due to the
geology, but it would be likely. Councilmember Bird asked if the City proceeded with the
recommended additional study, would the City expect to get this answered. Director Rigg said it
would.

Councilmember Goodhart asked what the current groundwater condition in MC Plaza is. Director
Rigg said there was a video taken in the sub-drain which showed only about 25-30% of the holes still
flowing. The groundwater is currently a little higher than usual compared to historical measurements.
There have been no recent damage complaints from the building owners. Bank of America upgraded
their pumps about four years ago. The other buildings have also upgraded their pumps.
Councilmember Goodhart asked if the study would recommend a corrective action. Director Rigg
believes it would be a similar process to the current Bluff Cove project. The City will survey the area,
develop potential solutions, figure potential costs, and then the City can weigh the benefits and
negatives of each. Director Rigg said he would not want to see the City pursue a replacement of an in
kind replacement of the sub-drain. Councilmember Goodhart said the charts show the water peaking in
May-June and he wondered if the sub-drain could manage an increase in groundwater. Director Rigg
said the question is whether it is the responsibility of a city to manage groundwater for local building
issues.

Mayor Perkins said the ownership of groundwater is relevant. She would like to know from a legal
perspective. She would like to know how much of the groundwater is due to irrigation and if state
mandated reductions will translate into reductions in flow of the groundwater. She believes the City
needs more information gathered in order to make decisions. She also wondered what any diversion of
the water flow would have on the local habitat.

Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey the MC Plaza groundwater problem has been around since the early
1990’s. She said it is a good question - whether the City should do anything about the groundwater.

Councilmember Rea said the report is interesting, from an engineering standpoint, in that the water can
be pumped to the Golf Course. He asked why in 1994 there was such a dramatic drop in the level of
groundwater. Director Rigg said it was due to the Northridge earthquake.

Ray Burns, [PVE P.O. Box], Managing Partner of Peninsula Investment Company (owners of two
buildings in MC Plaza) said the moment has arrived to investigate the groundwater with a
comprehensive study. He offered a copy of a 2001 thesis document written by a CSU Long Beach
student who was mentored by former PVE geologist Perry Ehlig titled ‘The Source Flow and
CITY COUNCIL  8
JANUARY 13, 2010
 Mitigation of Groundwater in the Malaga Cove Area.’ Mr. Burns believes the groundwater should be
intercepted at the source element prior to reaching Malaga Cove instead of pumping it out.

City Manager Hoefgen thanked the West Basin Water District and the Water Replenishment District
for funding the 2009 study.

There was Council discussion on what direction to undertake – how to define the problem and how to
address it.

Director Rigg believed the scope of any report would be a monitoring plan to try to understand the
sources, direction, the dynamics of the aquifer and then to figure out any solutions.

Councilmember Rea asked where the Golf Club is in their research. City Manager Hoefgen said the
Golf Club is conducting legal research regarding ownership of the water and whether they have the
right to access the water.

Mayor Perkins thought it would be worthwhile to include information about a potential
study/monitoring program in the upcoming budget. She would like part of the scope of the study to be
the expected outcome of the study, the purpose of the study, and what the City would want to take
away from it.

The Council would like to see a Budget Issue Paper for the study and monitoring of groundwater in
Malaga Cove Plaza.
